_comment: Prompt set for scripts/bench_agentic.py. Committed so a run is reproducible.
Allocation matches /frontier-refresh's FIXED quality weights, so a composite
computed from these rows is comparable with the frontier reports:
Prompts are drawn from what this fleet actually does — OpenClaw routing,
Home Assistant commands, transcript cleanup, Spanish voice notes, grocery —
not from generic benchmark sets. Published-benchmark verdicts have twice
failed to survive contact with this project's real domain (parakeet WER,
faster-whisper RTFx), so role-shaped prompts are the honest test.
Catalan coverage is uneven across all open models; those two rows are
flagged in the report rather than treated as equal-confidence evidence.
long_context rows synthesise a haystack from filler_words using a fixed
seed (see bench_agentic.FILLER_SEED) — byte-identical every run. The needle
sits at 60% depth, not at an edge where recall is trivial.

prompts.system: You are a terse ops assistant. Answer in at most 6 numbered steps.
prompts.user: A local FastAPI hub on port 8000 is serving stale code after an edit. It is started by a system-tray launcher that owns the process. Give the safe restart procedure and how to confirm the new build is actually live.

prompts.system: Summarise in exactly 3 bullets. No preamble.
prompts.user: The team migrated the transcription role from a GPU whisper instance on the main workstation to a Linux satellite box, freeing about two gigabytes of VRAM on the workstation. The satellite is slower — roughly nine times real time versus thirty-three — but transcription there is only a fallback path, since a Parakeet model on a Mac handles the primary load on its neural engine. The freed VRAM went to the agentic models. A later change moved the text-to-speech model back to the workstation because the satellite's older GPU rendered speech below real time, causing audible stutter.

prompts.system: Remove filler words and false starts. Keep the speaker's meaning and voice. Output only the cleaned text.
prompts.user: so um I was thinking that we could uh maybe move the the whisper thing to the other machine, you know, because like it's it's taking too much memory on this one, and uh honestly the the other box is just sitting there doing nothing most of the of the time right

prompts.system: Rewrite in a neutral, professional register. One paragraph. Output only the rewrite.
prompts.user: this is the third time the deploy has blown up because someone didn't bother checking whether the port was already bound. it's not hard. just look before you bind.

prompts.system: Convert to bullets. One bullet per distinct requirement. Output only the bullets.
prompts.user: The installer needs to check that the virtual environment exists, that the dependencies are installed, that a GPU is visible, that the vendored binaries have been downloaded, that the model weights are present, and that the ports it wants are free. Each check should report what is missing and offer a fix action.

prompts.system: Write a conventional-commit message: a subject line under 72 characters, a blank line, then 2-3 bullets explaining why rather than what. Output only the message.
prompts.user: The port-in-use check only looked at listeners bound to the specific address, so a process bound to the wildcard address 0.0.0.0 on the same port was not detected and the server would fail to start with a confusing error much later in the boot sequence.

prompts.system: Answer in under 120 words, plain prose, no bullets.
prompts.user: Explain the trade-off between keeping a large model always resident in GPU memory versus loading it on demand with an idle-unload timer, for a machine that also has to run a small always-on model and a speech synthesiser.
